# JK Flip-Flop – Assertion Based Verification (SystemVerilog)

## Overview

This project implements and verifies a synchronous **JK Flip-Flop** using **SystemVerilog**.

The primary focus is on **Assertion-Based Verification (ABV)** using SystemVerilog Assertions (SVA) and the `bind` methodology to verify functionality without modifying the DUT.

---

## Design Description

The JK Flip-Flop is implemented with:

- Positive-edge triggered clock
- Active-low synchronous reset (`rstn`)
- Standard JK behavior

### Functional Truth Table (Generated by AI)

| J | K | Operation | Next Q |
|---|---|-----------|--------|
| 0 | 0 | Hold      | Q      |
| 0 | 1 | Reset     | 0      |
| 1 | 0 | Set       | 1      |
| 1 | 1 | Toggle    | ~Q     |

---

## Verification Strategy Used 

Verification is performed using **SystemVerilog Assertions (SVA)**.

- Assertions are written in a separate module to understand the working properly
- `bind` is used for attaching Assertion module to DUT in testbench.
- Functional behavior is verified at every clock edge
- State-based checking to ensures correctness of the design.

### Assertions Used to Verify the design

- Global reset verification
- Reset state (J=0, K=1)
- Set state (J=1, K=0)
- Hold condition check (J=0, K=0)
- Toggle condition check (J=1, K=1)

---

## Tools & Languages Used

- SystemVerilog
- SystemVerilog Assertions (SVA)
- Temporal(Time related) operators (`|=>`, `$past`, `$stable`)
- Bind methodology
- Simulation-based verification

---

- Writing effective state-based assertions for any Filp-Flop
- Understanding temporal verification logic
